rows: A built-in sample of three decoded TABLE_DUMP_V2 RIB routes — browse it to learn the reader's output columns without supplying an MRT file.

rows.vgi.doc_llm: A zero-setup preview of the row shape read_rib produces: three routes decoded from a tiny TABLE_DUMP_V2 RIB fixture bundled into the worker. Browse it directly — a plain no-argument scan — to see real decoded columns like timestamp, RIB view name, reporting peer (IP as INET, and ASN), prefix (INET), origin ASN, AS path, next hop (INET), and communities before you have a file in hand. It takes no arguments and always returns the same three rows. For real data call read_rib / read_updates with a path or URL; this view is only a self-describing example.
rows.vgi.doc_md: A built-in, no-arguments sample of three decoded TABLE_DUMP_V2 RIB routes, so you can browse `bgp.main.example_rib` to learn the reader's output columns without an MRT file. Cast the INET columns (`peer_ip`, `prefix`, `next_hop`) with `::INET`. Point read_rib at your own archive for real data.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Group the built-in sample routes by origin AS to see how many prefixes each announced.","sql":"SELECT origin_asn, count(*) AS routes FROM bgp.main.example_rib GROUP BY origin_asn ORDER BY routes DESC, origin_asn;"}]
rows.vgi.title: Sample RIB Routes
